---SIGNAL 1---
NAME: Net-Cash Profit Reliability
EXPRESSION: MUL(IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(che,ADD(dltt,dlc)),MUL(prcc_f,csho)),1)),IND_RANK(WINSOR(SUB(MA(RATIO(SUB(oibdp,dp),at),3),VOL(RATIO(SUB(oibdp,dp),at),3)),1)))
HYPOTHESIS: Firms with high net cash relative to market value outperform when post-depreciation operating profitability is consistently strong.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: Netting debt from cash avoids treating highly leveraged cash balances as equivalent to unencumbered equity valuation support. The matched mean-minus-volatility profitability measure provides a smooth reliability adjustment, testing whether the strong cash-backing result survives beyond a single worst-year floor construction.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 2---
NAME: Enterprise Cash Conversion Floor
EXPRESSION: MUL(IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(ADD(oancf,xint),ADD(MUL(prcc_f,csho),SUB(ADD(dltt,dlc),che))),1)),IND_RANK(WINSOR(TS_MIN(RATIO(oiadp,SUB(revt,cogs)),3),1)))
HYPOTHESIS: Firms with high pre-interest operating cash flow relative to enterprise value outperform when gross profit has consistently converted into operating income.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: The valuation leg aligns pre-interest cash generation with the market value of all capital claims. Using the worst recent gross-to-operating conversion ratio tests whether downside cost discipline, rather than average conversion, protects enterprise-cash bargains from becoming value traps.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional

---SIGNAL 3---
NAME: Accelerating-Profit Earnings Value
EXPRESSION: MUL(IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(ni,MUL(prcc_f,csho)),1)),IND_RANK(WINSOR(ADD(RATIO(oiadp,at),ACCEL(RATIO(oiadp,at))),1)))
HYPOTHESIS: High net-income-yield firms outperform when operating return on assets is both high and accelerating.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: Adding profitability acceleration to the current level prevents improving but still deeply unprofitable firms from receiving an attractive quality score. This tests whether changes in the speed of fundamental improvement provide information beyond the previously successful peak-drawdown mechanism.
INTERACTION_TYPE: novel

---SIGNAL 4---
NAME: Cumulative-Cash Margin Floor
EXPRESSION: MUL(IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(TS_SUM(oancf,3),MUL(prcc_f,csho)),1)),IND_RANK(WINSOR(TS_MIN(RATIO(oiadp,sale),3),1)))
HYPOTHESIS: Firms priced cheaply relative to cumulative operating cash generation outperform when operating margins remain strong even in their weakest recent year.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: Three-year cumulative cash flow reduces sensitivity to a temporarily elevated current cash-flow yield and represents sustained internally generated value. The operating-margin floor separately requires durable pricing and cost economics, so the construction does not collapse into a single current profit-to-price ratio.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional

---SIGNAL 5---
NAME: Intangible-Productivity Enterprise Value
EXPRESSION: MUL(IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(ebitda,ADD(MUL(prcc_f,csho),SUB(ADD(dltt,dlc),che))),1)),IND_RANK(WINSOR(ADD(RATIO(ADD(oiadp,COALESCE(xrd,SUB(revt,revt))),ADD(at,TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd,SUB(revt,revt)),3))),DELTA(RATIO(ADD(oiadp,COALESCE(xrd,SUB(revt,revt))),ADD(at,TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd,SUB(revt,revt)),3))),1)),1)))
HYPOTHESIS: Cheap enterprises outperform when returns on tangible plus recently accumulated R&D capital are high and improving.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: Recent R&D is incorporated into the productive-capital denominator while current R&D is restored to operating income, producing an intangible-inclusive return measure. Unlike an intangible-adjusted book-value sort, the interaction tests whether the level and improvement of R&D-capital productivity validate conventional enterprise cheapness.
INTERACTION_TYPE: novel

---SIGNAL 6---
NAME: Fixed-Charge-Covered Earnings Value
EXPRESSION: MUL(IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(ib,MUL(prcc_f,csho)),1)),IND_RANK(WINSOR(SUB(MA(RATIO(oibdp,ADD(xint,dp)),3),VOL(RATIO(oibdp,ADD(xint,dp)),3)),1)))
HYPOTHESIS: High earnings-yield firms outperform when operating cash earnings reliably cover both interest expense and depreciation.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: Operating profit before depreciation relative to interest plus depreciation measures coverage of financing costs and recurring asset consumption. Its mean-minus-volatility form favors consistently covered firms, providing a fixed-charge resilience mechanism rather than another asset-scaled profitability floor.
INTERACTION_TYPE: ratio

---CRITIQUE Net-Cash Profit Reliability---
VERDICT: accept
SCORE: 3
RATIONALE: Netting debt from the cash-backing leg and replacing the worst-year floor with a mean-minus-volatility reliability measure are both economically substantive changes to the archive's best performer rather than pure cosmetics, though the signal remains within the same cash-value × profitability-durability family and its incremental content over "Cash-Backed Profit Floor" may be small.

---CRITIQUE Enterprise Cash Conversion Floor---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 2
RATIONALE: This is a one-operator swap (MA→TS_MIN on the identical conversion ratio) on an identical valuation leg from the archived "Enterprise Cash Conversion Value," i.e., a cosmetic variant rather than a new mechanism.

---CRITIQUE Accelerating-Profit Earnings Value---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 2
RATIONALE: The stated "high and accelerating" hypothesis is not what the expression computes, since a second-difference ACCEL term is an order of magnitude smaller than the ROA level it is added to, so the quality leg collapses to plain ROA and the signal degenerates into a near-duplicate of the archived earnings-yield × profitability constructions.

---CRITIQUE Cumulative-Cash Margin Floor---
VERDICT: accept
SCORE: 3
RATIONALE: Three-year cumulative operating cash flow scaled by price is a defensible smoothing of the classic cash-flow-to-price anomaly and the margin floor is a distinct conditioning variable, but the value × quality-floor template is already heavily sampled in the archive so expected incremental information is modest.

---CRITIQUE Intangible-Productivity Enterprise Value---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 2
RATIONALE: It reuses an EBITDA/EV leg that already produced negligible FF5 alpha in two archived variants, and the "high and improving" claim is undercut by adding a small DELTA term to a much larger level term, so the conditioning leg is effectively just an intangible-adjusted return level at considerable expression complexity.

---CRITIQUE Fixed-Charge-Covered Earnings Value---
VERDICT: accept
SCORE: 4
RATIONALE: Fixed-charge coverage (oibdp over interest plus depreciation) is a genuinely different conditioning dimension from the asset-scaled profitability floors already tested, the mean-minus-volatility form matches the stated "reliably cover" hypothesis, and the expected positive sign follows naturally from the construction.

---SIGNAL 1---
NAME: Ex-Cash Operating Franchise Value
EXPRESSION: MUL(IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(ceq,che),SUB(MUL(prcc_f,csho),che)),1)),IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(oiadp,SUB(at,che)),1)))
HYPOTHESIS: Firms whose operating businesses are cheap after stripping out cash outperform when their noncash operating assets generate strong profits.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
INTERACTION_TYPE: ratio
REASONING: Removing cash from book equity, market value, and total assets isolates the valuation and profitability of the operating franchise rather than rewarding cash holdings themselves. The matched construction requires the ex-cash business to be both inexpensive and productive, replacing the archived enterprise-cash conversion mechanism.

---SIGNAL 2---
NAME: Rank-Balanced Profit Acceleration Value
EXPRESSION: MUL(IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(ni,MUL(prcc_f,csho)),1)),MIN(IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(oiadp,at),1)),IND_RANK(WINSOR(ACCEL(RATIO(oiadp,at)),1))))
HYPOTHESIS: High net-income-yield firms outperform when operating return on assets is both high and accelerating.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional
REASONING: Profitability level and acceleration are ranked separately before taking their minimum, giving acceleration equal cross-sectional influence instead of allowing its smaller numerical scale to disappear. The quality score can be high only when both the level and change-of-change dimensions are strong, making this a genuine acceleration-conditioned value signal.

---SIGNAL 3---
NAME: Liquidity-Backed Intangible Productivity
EXPRESSION: MUL(IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(che,dlc),MUL(prcc_f,csho)),1)),MIN(IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(ADD(oiadp,COALESCE(xrd,SUB(revt,revt))),ADD(at,TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd,SUB(revt,revt)),3))),1)),IND_RANK(WINSOR(DELTA(RATIO(ADD(oiadp,COALESCE(xrd,SUB(revt,revt))),ADD(at,TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd,SUB(revt,revt)),3))),1),1))))
HYPOTHESIS: Firms with substantial liquidity net of short-term debt outperform when returns on tangible plus recent R&D capital are both high and improving.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
INTERACTION_TYPE: novel
REASONING: Cash net of current debt measures near-term funding capacity rather than reusing the low-alpha EBITDA-to-enterprise-value leg. Separately ranking the level and change in intangible-inclusive profitability makes improvement a binding condition, while the three-year R&D stock links that condition to the productivity of funded intangible investment.
